subject: general
question:
**Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select No error’.**

He belted two huge sixers, but / eleven to get of the last two / deliveries was a big ask

options.text: eleven to get of the last two
He belted two huge sixers, but

solution:
The erroneous part of the sentence is: "**eleven to get of the last two.**"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase "**eleven to get of the last two**" is grammatically **incorrect**.
 
• '**Of**' is used to show a relationship or connection between someone or something to another.
 
• '**Off**' means away from someone or something, i.e. it expresses the act detachment from a person, place or object.
 
• The correct phrase should be "**eleven to get off the last two**" to indicate the number of runs required to win. (Hindi: जीतने के लिए चाहिए होने वाले गेंदों की संख्या)
 
 
• **For example-** *They needed eleven runs to get off the last two deliveries.*
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 1**.

**Corrected sentence:** *He belted two huge sixers, but eleven to get **off **the last two deliveries was a big ask.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Option 2: "**Deliveries was a big ask**" This part of the sentence is also **grammatically correct**. It refers to the difficult task of scoring a certain number of runs in the remaining deliveries.
 
• Option 4: "**He belted two huge sixers, but**" This part of the sentence is **grammatically correct**. It indicates that the person hit two sixes.
